author: GamingBolt
description:
From the mind and team behind games like Summerland and Dread X Collection 5’s We Never Left comes a brand new psychological horror experience, Project Songbird. The story largely focuses on a single character, Dakota, who has been suffering from writer’s block, resulting in her latest musical release getting bad reviews just about everywhere. In her attempt to fix this, she decides to spend a month in a remote cabin in the Appalachian woods, completely disconnected from the outside world.

The horror gameplay of Project Songbird is far from revolutionary; you will spend much of your time walking around, exploring your surroundings, and solving simple puzzles. Every now and then, however, you will also have to take on strange creatures and experience surreal shifts in reality that are bound to leave you dumbfounded. author: GamingBolt
description:
Crimson Desert might not have stuck the landing as well as it hoped with its launch. The game has issues that have put off more than a few players from experiencing the depth and scale of what it has hidden away in the lands of Pywel. 

That's a shame because those who've managed to stick with it enough swear by its quality. It's a paradox that might be hard to navigate for a studio but the initial round of fixes has us very optimistic about the game's chances. 

Why do we think so? We're here to take you through it. Join us on a look into why Crimson Desert's patches matter, and why the ones that come next matter even more!

title: Crimson Desert Could Soon Become A BEAST of A Game
